sdid: Updated Synthetic Difference-in-Differences Estimation and Inference for R

Source: R/synthdid-package.R
sdid-package.Rd

Synthetic difference-in-differences (Arkhangelsky et al. 2021) for the average effect of a treatment on the treated in panel data, with synthetic control and difference-in-differences in the same framework, in the manner of the Stata command sdid of Clarke, Pailañir, Athey and Imbens (2024). Designs where treated units adopt treatment in the same period or in different periods are both supported, with bootstrap, jackknife and placebo inference, covariate adjustment by either of the Stata command's two methods, and estimation in compiled code with parallel replications.

Estimation goes through sdid(), which takes a panel in long format and returns a result with a Stata-style table. The result can be passed to sdid_plot(), sdid_units_plot(), sdid_placebo() and sdid_placebo_plot().

The package derives from synthdid 0.0.9 by Dmitry Arkhangelsky, Susan Athey, David A. Hirshberg, Guido W. Imbens and Stefan Wager.

Details

Package options

  • sdid.num.threads sets the number of threads used for bootstrap, jackknife and placebo replications. When unset, all available hardware threads are used. The num.threads argument of sdid() overrides it. Results do not depend on the thread count.

  • sdid.solver selects how the Frank-Wolfe weight solver computes its gradient. "auto" (the default) starts with the direct method and switches to a precomputed Gram matrix once a solve has run as many iterations as it has weights. "direct" never switches and reproduces the results of synthdid 0.0.9 up to rounding. "gram" uses the Gram matrix from the first iteration. Estimates with covariates adjusted by the optimized method always use the direct method.

  • sdid.gram.max.mb caps the size of the Gram matrix, in megabytes, defaulting to 64. Solves whose Gram matrix would exceed it use the direct method.

Examples

# \donttest{
# The effect of California's Proposition 99 on cigarette consumption.
data(california_prop99)
fit = sdid(california_prop99, "PacksPerCapita", "State", "Year",
           "treated", vce = "placebo", seed = 1213, graph = FALSE)
#> 
#> Synthetic Difference-in-Differences Estimator
#> 
#> Outcome     PacksPerCapita
#> Treatment   treated
#> Units       39 (38 never treated, 1 treated)
#> Periods     31 (1970 to 2000), treatment from 1989
#> Inference   placebo, 50 replications
#> 
#> 
#>               ATT Std. Err.     z P>|z| [95% Conf. Interval]
#> treated -15.60383  10.93638 -1.43 0.154  -37.03873   5.83108
#> 
#> 95% confidence intervals and p-values use the normal approximation.
coef(fit)
#>   treated 
#> -15.60383 
confint(fit)
#>             2.5 %   97.5 %
#> treated -37.03873 5.831077
# }
